name: coverage-driver
//: The two coverage drivers and their self-tests: coverage.sh (the per-crate instrumented test runs and the merged report the coverage gate project runs) and shcov.sh with shcov.rb (bashcov around each shell-measured project's tests, and the merged shell report the shell-coverage gate runs). Nothing depends on it but the two gates. The Rust gate needs only the driver itself, so a product edit never selects these self-tests through it; the shell gate merges this project's own record too (its tests run both drivers' scripts), so its dependsOn runs them — a few seconds over a scratch workspace.
//suppression-tags: llmlint: ignore-block[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge] coverage-driver's whole test suite is cheap, not an expensive tier: its Rust-driver half (coverage.test.mjs) builds two dependency-free scratch crates offline into a fresh CARGO_TARGET_DIR on every run, so it is always cold, and measured 2.25s that way; the shell gate must merge this project's record because those same tests are what execute coverage.sh

test.//suppression: llmlint: ignore-block[shell_test_tiers_stay_split] this project holds only the two coverage drivers, coverage.sh (cargo-llvm-cov and nextest) and shcov.sh/shcov.rb (bashcov), which exist only to drive those tools; the suite runs each real tool over a scratch workspace, offline, so its offline and its host-tool tiers are the same thing, no unrelated script edit can pay for it, and only an edit to a driver (or the cargo/cargo-llvm-cov/nextest versions and the shell coverage pins, inputs of this cached target) reruns it

options.command: bash tools/coverage/shcov.sh run coverage-driver -- bun test --timeout 600000 tools/coverage/tests

test.//: Both drivers against scratch inputs under the real tools: profiles combine across crates and the Rust floor fails below 95%; a shell record merges across projects, counts a scratch copy of a script for the script, and the shell floor fails below its bar; bad input is a usage error.
